name: Kenshiro
summary: A musculoskeletal humanoid from the University of Tokyo's JSK lab built to copy human anatomy: an aluminum skeleton driven by about 160 pulley-and-cable 'muscles' arranged like real ones, with a flexible spine. Kenshiro is a platform for studying how the human body's structure enables its movement.
notable: ~160 tendon 'muscles', the most of any humanoid at the time
